intro.codingAgents: Each check earns a share of its weight (critical 10, high 7, medium 4, low 2; a warning earns part of it). The score is the weight earned over the weight of the checks that ran, out of 100. Some critical failures cap the score: with no llms.txt it is at most 59.

codingAgents.label: llms.txt exists
codingAgents.measures: Whether llms.txt is discoverable at any of the candidate locations.
codingAgents.why: Coding agents look for llms.txt to find the right page. Without it they guess URLs. AFDocs caps the score at 59 when it is missing.

codingAgents.label: llms.txt format
codingAgents.measures: Whether llms.txt follows the proposed structure from llmstxt.org.
codingAgents.why: A predictable structure (an H1, then Markdown links) is what agents and tools parse.

codingAgents.label: llms.txt size
codingAgents.measures: Whether llms.txt fits within agent truncation limits.
codingAgents.why: Agents read about 100,000 characters per fetch; a larger index is cut off.

codingAgents.label: llms.txt links resolve
codingAgents.measures: Whether the URLs listed in llms.txt actually resolve.
codingAgents.why: A broken link in the index sends an agent to a dead end.

codingAgents.label: llms.txt links point to Markdown
codingAgents.measures: Whether the URLs in llms.txt point to markdown content.
codingAgents.why: Markdown is far smaller than HTML, so more of the page fits in what the agent reads.

codingAgents.label: Page points agents to llms.txt (HTML)
codingAgents.measures: Whether HTML pages include a directive pointing to llms.txt.
codingAgents.why: An agent that lands on one page learns where the index of the whole site is.

codingAgents.label: Page points agents to llms.txt (Markdown)
codingAgents.measures: Whether markdown pages include a directive pointing to llms.txt.
codingAgents.why: Agents that read the Markdown copy see the pointer too.

codingAgents.label: .md version of the page
codingAgents.measures: Whether appending .md to page URLs returns valid markdown.
codingAgents.why: Agents guess <page>.md; a Markdown copy is much smaller than the HTML.
codingAgents.host: A rewrite from <page> to <page>.md can be set by your host rather than your build. A local build (`--dir` or a localhost URL) counts this check, but your host can change the result.

codingAgents.label: Markdown on request
codingAgents.measures: Whether the server responds to Accept: text/markdown.
codingAgents.why: Claude Code, Cursor and OpenCode ask for Markdown first.
codingAgents.host: Your web server or CDN decides what to return for Accept: text/markdown. A local build (`--dir` or a localhost URL) doesn't count this check.

codingAgents.label: Content without JavaScript
codingAgents.measures: Whether pages contain server-rendered content or are client-side rendered SPA shells.
codingAgents.why: AI crawlers and most coding agents do not run JavaScript, so content rendered in the browser is invisible to them.

codingAgents.label: Markdown size
codingAgents.measures: Character count of page when served as markdown.
codingAgents.why: Agents read about 100,000 characters per fetch and have to page or give up beyond it.

codingAgents.label: HTML size
codingAgents.measures: Character count of HTML response and post-conversion size.
codingAgents.why: Agents that read HTML convert it to text; past about 100,000 characters the rest is cut off.

codingAgents.label: Download size
codingAgents.measures: Served byte size of the HTML document after transfer decoding.
codingAgents.why: Very large documents can exceed an agent's fetch buffer before any text is read.

codingAgents.label: Content starts near the top
codingAgents.measures: How far into content the actual documentation begins.
codingAgents.why: Navigation before the content uses up the part of the page an agent reads first.

codingAgents.label: Complete in one fetch
codingAgents.measures: Whether markdown responses are complete in one fetch or declare a working continuation.
codingAgents.why: An agent that gets half a page and no way to the rest works from half the facts.

codingAgents.label: Tabbed content readable
codingAgents.measures: Whether tabbed/accordion content serializes into oversized output.
codingAgents.why: Tabs flatten into one long text for an agent; every variant counts toward the size limit.

codingAgents.label: Headers inside tabs
codingAgents.measures: Whether headers in tabbed sections include variant context.
codingAgents.why: Flattened tabs repeat the same headings; without the variant name an agent can't tell them apart.

codingAgents.label: Code fences closed
codingAgents.measures: Whether markdown contains unclosed code fences.
codingAgents.why: An unclosed fence turns the rest of the page into code for the agent.

codingAgents.label: Links work outside the site
codingAgents.measures: Whether links in served markdown are absolute and resolve to what they promise.
codingAgents.why: Relative links break once the Markdown is read outside the site, as agents do.

codingAgents.label: Embedded data size
codingAgents.measures: Whether machine-generated bulk data (large tables, data blobs) dominates oversized pages.
codingAgents.why: Bulk data can push the actual explanation past what an agent reads.

codingAgents.label: Real 404s for missing pages
codingAgents.measures: Whether error pages return correct HTTP status codes.
codingAgents.why: A "not found" page served with 200 looks like real content to an agent.
codingAgents.host: Status codes for missing pages are set by your web server or host. A local build (`--dir` or a localhost URL) doesn't count this check.

codingAgents.label: Redirects
codingAgents.measures: Whether redirects are same-host HTTP redirects.
codingAgents.why: Cross-host or JavaScript redirects lose agents that follow links.
codingAgents.host: Redirects are configured on your host or CDN. A local build (`--dir` or a localhost URL) doesn't count this check.

codingAgents.label: llms.txt covers the sitemap
codingAgents.measures: How much of the site is represented in llms.txt.
codingAgents.why: Pages missing from the index are found less often. Lensy skips it: it is about the whole site, not the page.

codingAgents.label: Markdown matches HTML
codingAgents.measures: Whether markdown and HTML versions contain equivalent content.
codingAgents.why: A Markdown copy that drops content gives agents a different page than people see.

codingAgents.label: Cache headers
codingAgents.measures: Whether cache headers allow timely updates.
codingAgents.why: Long caching keeps agents reading old versions after you fix a page.
codingAgents.host: Cache headers are set by your web server or CDN. A local build (`--dir` or a localhost URL) doesn't count this check.

codingAgents.label: Public without login
codingAgents.measures: Whether documentation pages require authentication to access content.
codingAgents.why: Agents can't log in, so gated docs are invisible to them.
codingAgents.host: Login walls are enforced by your host. A local build (`--dir` or a localhost URL) doesn't count this check.

codingAgents.label: Alternative access to gated docs
codingAgents.measures: Whether an auth-gated documentation site provides alternative access paths for agents.
codingAgents.why: When docs need a login, an alternative path lets agents read them anyway.
codingAgents.host: Access rules are enforced by your host. A local build (`--dir` or a localhost URL) doesn't count this check.

codingAgents.label: Bot protection lets agents in
codingAgents.measures: Whether bot-protection systems interfere with automated fetching of documentation content.
codingAgents.why: Bot protection that refuses honest agents keeps the docs out of their answers.
codingAgents.host: Bot protection runs on your host or CDN, not in your build. A local build (`--dir` or a localhost URL) doesn't count this check.

codingAgents.label: Headings an agent can navigate
codingAgents.measures: On what an agent receives: exactly one H1 (half the points; more than one, a fifth) and an outline with no skipped heading levels (half; one skip, a quarter), counted only with at least 2 headings.
codingAgents.why: A URL #fragment never reaches the server, so agents find sections by heading text. AFDocs' section-header-quality only looks inside tabs.

evidence.title: How Claude Code eats the web

fallback.label: Content without JavaScript
fallback.measures: Words in the raw HTML after removing scripts, styles, navigation, asides and site-chrome headers. 150 or more words with no empty app root: full points. 40 to 149 words: half. Fewer: none.
fallback.why: AI crawlers and most coding agents fetch the HTML and do not run JavaScript, so content rendered in the browser is invisible to them.

evidence.title: Do AI crawlers render JavaScript (Vercel and MERJ data, via SearchOptimo)

fallback.label: Markdown on request
fallback.measures: A GET of the page with Accept: text/markdown returns Markdown (a Markdown or plain-text content type, Markdown structure, not HTML).
fallback.why: Claude Code, Cursor and OpenCode ask for Markdown first. Markdown is far smaller than the HTML of the same page, so more of it fits in what the agent reads.
fallback.host: Your web server or CDN decides what to return for Accept: text/markdown. A local build (`--dir` or a localhost URL) doesn't count this check.

evidence.title: Do AI agents read Markdown (Checkly data, via GoodBarber)

fallback.label: .md version discoverable
fallback.measures: A Markdown copy exists (rel=alternate, a Link header, or <url>.md) and is advertised (rel=alternate, a Link header, or listed in llms.txt): full points. Exists but not advertised: 8.
fallback.why: Agents guess .md URLs and follow llms.txt. A copy nothing points to is found less often.
fallback.host: A Link header advertising the Markdown copy, or a rewrite to <page>.md, is set by your host. A local build (`--dir` or a localhost URL) counts this check, but your host can change the result.

fallback.label: llms.txt usable
fallback.measures: llms.txt found at the root or docs path and not HTML: 8. Valid format (an H1 and Markdown links): 4. Sampled links resolve, up to 8 checked: 4 times the share. Size up to 50K characters: 4; up to 100K: 2.
fallback.why: Coding agents use llms.txt to find the right page. AI crawlers do not request it, so it counts for coding agents only.

fallback.label: Page fits one fetch
fallback.measures: Size of what an agent receives (Markdown when offered, otherwise the HTML text): up to 50K characters 15, up to 100K 10, more 0. Under 40 words received: 0.
fallback.why: Agents read a limited window per fetch, about 100,000 characters, and have to page or give up beyond it.

evidence.title: How Claude Code eats the web

fallback.label: Sections findable
fallback.measures: On what the agent receives: exactly one H1 5 (more than one 2). No heading-level skips 6 (one skip 3), counted only with at least 2 headings. Share of H2/H3 with id attributes times 4.
fallback.why: A URL #fragment never reaches the server, so agents fetch the whole page and find sections by heading text.

evidence.title: How Claude Code eats the web

aiSearch.label: AI search bots allowed
aiSearch.measures: 20 times the share of six AI search and retrieval bots (OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User, PerplexityBot, Perplexity-User, Claude-SearchBot, Claude-User) that robots.txt allows for this path. Most specific group, longest matching rule wins.
aiSearch.why: These bots fetch pages for ChatGPT search, Perplexity and Claude answers. A page they may not fetch cannot be cited.

aiSearch.label: Content without JavaScript
aiSearch.measures: Words in the raw HTML after removing scripts, styles, navigation, asides and site-chrome headers. 150 or more words with no empty app root: full points. 40 to 149 words: half. Fewer: none.
aiSearch.why: AI crawlers and most coding agents fetch the HTML and do not run JavaScript, so content rendered in the browser is invisible to them.

evidence.title: Do AI crawlers render JavaScript (Vercel and MERJ data, via SearchOptimo)

aiSearch.label: Indexable
aiSearch.measures: Not noindex (meta robots or X-Robots-Tag): 10, and noindex makes the whole check 0. Canonical present: 7. Page listed in the sitemap: 8. Sitemaps named in robots.txt are used; without one, Lensy tries <link rel="sitemap">, /sitemap.xml and /sitemap-index.xml, then the same under the page's first path segment (for example /docs/sitemap.xml). Sitemap indexes are followed, at most 12 files.
aiSearch.why: A page that asks not to be indexed, or that search engines cannot find in the sitemap, is less likely to be retrieved for an answer.
aiSearch.host: An X-Robots-Tag noindex header is set by your host. A local build (`--dir` or a localhost URL) counts this check, but your host can change the result.

evidence.title: arXiv 2609.35077: what drives citations in production LLMs

aiSearch.label: Freshness declared
aiSearch.measures: A date in the raw HTML (dateModified, article:modified_time, <time datetime> or visible "Last updated" text): 6. This URL's sitemap entry has lastmod: 4. Sitemap lastmod values are not all identical: 3. Page date and lastmod agree within 7 days: 2. Age is shown, not scored.
aiSearch.why: Recency is a consistent secondary signal for AI citations, and search engines use sitemap lastmod only when it is believable.

aiSearch.label: Answer-ready sections
aiSearch.measures: On the HTML: one H1 4 (more than one 2). No heading skips 4 (one skip 2), counted only with at least 2 headings. Median words per H2/H3 section: 40 to 500 7; under 40 or 501 to 900 4; over 900 1; no sections 0.
aiSearch.why: AI search retrieves passages of about a heading plus its paragraphs, so each section should answer one question on its own.

aiSearch.label: JSON-LD
aiSearch.measures: Parseable JSON-LD with an @type: 3. Has dateModified: 2.
aiSearch.why: Controlled studies found structured data barely moves AI citations, so it carries few points. dateModified also declares freshness.
